The linear system in \(a,b,c\) is
\[
\begin{aligned}
(x-2)a-b-c&=0,\\
-a+(y-2)b-c&=0,\\
-a-b+(z-2)c&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(a,b,c\) are nonzero, the determinant must be zero:
\[
\begin{vmatrix}
x-2 & -1 & -1\\
-1 & y-2 & -1\\
-1 & -1 & z-2
\end{vmatrix}=0.
\]
This gives
\[
(x-2)(y-2)(z-2)-(x-2)-(y-2)-(z-2)-2=0.
\]
Since \(x+y+z=3\), we have
\[
(x-2)+(y-2)+(z-2)=3-6=-3.
\]
Thus
\[
(x-2)(y-2)(z-2)+3-2=0,
\]
so
\[
(x-2)(y-2)(z-2)=-1.
\]
Expanding,
\[
xyz-2(xy+xz+yz)+4(x+y+z)-8=-1.
\]
Using \(xy+xz+yz=5\) and \(x+y+z=3\),
\[
xyz-10+12-8=-1,
\]
so
\[
xyz-6=-1.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\boxed{5}.
\]
